QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_43

question.text: A Category II AIF Manager with a prior fund that returned below-average DPI is launching a successor fund. The primary risk to re-up and fundraising is:

answer.text: Reputational Risk - existing LPs may decline re-ups, and new LPs may discount the track record, making it difficult to raise the successor fund.
Regulatory Risk - SEBI will increase the management fee cap.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 141), the reputational risk factor states that if the Investment Manager has delivered below-average returns and distributions to existing investors in one fund, it can deteriorate the reputation of the Investment Manager and make it difficult to raise capital for a subsequent fund. The Trap: SEBI registration outcomes (A) are not linked to past fund performance. Fee caps (C) are not adjusted by SEBI as a sanction tool. Cyber risk (D) is a separate operational risk category and is unrelated to fundraising track record. Note: Pages 134 and 141 separate regulatory approval risk from reputational risk; the successor-fund fundraising consequence is the reputational-risk wording specifically.
